body:
Dedupe words: `PER_CHUNK_GZIP_CEILINGS framework` · `re-pin ceiling down` · `0.6388x headroom` · `check-eager-closure-budget` · `types-zod chunk`

Filed by the `domain:ui#2` execution seat (PM session `session_018HrVaotisyhgmot9o2MLRq`) as a **sub-issue of #10065**, whose domain it inherits — the in-flight derivation exception, ⛔ not a lane routing decision. ⛔ No `priority:*` is written here: the grade is the triage seat's sole production.

## The reading

PR #10082 (objectui#10065) moved the nine `packages/types/src/zod/**` validators out of the eager closure. The `framework` chunk went **69,560 → 41,782** gzipped in the same act. Its ceiling did not move, and nothing in that PR should have moved it — the dispatch forbade touching any ceiling, baseline or exemption constant, and the implementing dev correctly declined and reported it instead.

The consequence, stated as the gate itself states its own scale:

| | before #10082 | after #10082 |
|---|---|---|
| `PER_CHUNK_GZIP_CEILINGS.framework` | 100,000 | 100,000 |
| live measurement | 69,560 | 41,782 |
| headroom | 30,440 | **58,218** |
| headroom as a multiple of the regression this gate exists to catch | 0.3340x | **0.6388x** |

`scripts/check-eager-closure-budget.mjs`'s own header, verbatim (seat-read on `origin/main`):

> objectui#5266 was 89 KiB = 91,136 bytes, and this ceiling is built […] the headroom past ~89 KiB would leave the gate green through a repeat of

⇒ 58,218 / 91,136 = 0.6388. The row is now **most of a repeat of #5266 away** from red. ⛔ Nothing is broken; the gate still works. What changed is its RESOLUTION: a regression that would have been caught before can now hide under the headroom, and the change that bought the saving is what bought the blind spot.

## ⭐ The file already documents this exact move, twice, so the shape is not being invented here

The header carries its own precedent sections — 「Why `framework` moved (objectui#6759)」, 「Why `framework` moved again — objectui#7173」, and 「**Why `framework` moved DOWN, and where its bytes went — objectui#7399**」. The last one is this card's shape. It also records the convention a re-pin follows rather than widens:

> headroom convention rather than widening it: 9,137 bytes (0.10x)

⇒ the question is ⛔ not whether to re-pin, it is to WHAT. A 0.10x-convention pin over the new measurement is the obvious candidate; the deliverable is to take the measurement, pick the pin against the convention, and write the header section that says which build it was anchored to.

## ⚠️ `PER_CHUNK_BASELINE.framework` is a separate decision, and this card does not presume it

The baseline reads **72,245** and is likewise far above the live measurement. It is a HISTORICAL reading anchored to its own build, and the sensitivity leg does not read it. ⛔ Do not move it as a rider. If the taking dev concludes it should move, that is its own sentence with its own reason — ⛔ not a side effect of re-pinning the ceiling.

## ⚠️ Sequencing, which is real and must be checked at the top of the flight

Two open PRs touch this measurement:

- **#10082** — the change that produced the new figure. The measurement above is only valid once it is on `main`.
- **#9488** — also moves console chunking, and additionally asserts that `packages/types` lands WHOLLY in `framework`, which #10082 makes false. Whichever of the two lands second owes that assertion an update.

⇒ ⭐ **Re-measure `framework` on `origin/main` at the moment this card is taken.** ⛔ Do not re-use 41,782 from this card: it was measured on #10082's head, and if #9488 has landed in between, the figure has moved again and a pin set from this number would be pinned to a build that never existed.

## Acceptance

- The new ceiling is derived from a measurement taken in the taking act, with the build that produced it named.
- The convention the pin follows is stated (the file's own 0.10x headroom convention, or an argued alternative — ⛔ not an unexplained round number).
- A header section is added in the same shape as the three that precede it, saying which PR moved the chunk and where the bytes went.
- ⭐ The pin is proven to BITE: a counterfactual showing the gate red just above the new ceiling, with the mutation proven on disk and the restore proven by content — ⛔ never by an exit code. A ceiling nothing has ever seen refuse is a number, not a gate.

## Why it is worth a card rather than a rider on #10082

Re-pinning a gate's ceiling is a change to gate STRENGTH in the tightening direction, and the standing discipline keeps those out of the PR that motivated them: a saving PR that also moves the gate measuring it cannot be reviewed as either one.
